parallel.requirements: Recognized the prompt requirement to produce pure Node.js ESM .mjs files in /output, manually parse --a/--b/--c, avoid external dependencies, reproduce schedule.every job behavior, and match executable stdout/stderr behavior.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: Parent began probing, spawned /root/probe_exec for extra executable edge cases, and that child spawned /root/probe_exec/probe_exec; implementation ownership overlapped because parent and first child both wrote /output/test12.mjs and schedule modules.
parallel.implementation: Parent created an initial parser/text/timing/registry implementation, while the child created python_int/argparse_compat plus schedule modules; parent then patched the active child-style implementation for argparse behavior and entrypoint program-name handling.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: Parent noticed conflicting files in /output, chose the close child-style implementation, patched it, removed duplicate dead modules, and delivered test12.mjs with local library files.
parallel.verification: Parent and children compared executable output for normal runs, help/errors, repeated flags, invalid ints, nonpositive intervals, and unknown args; the parent ran a representative diff harness that ended OK.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: No official unfinished requirement remained; the only observed defect at closure was resolved coordination churn from overlapping generated implementations.

serial.requirements: Recognized the same ESM, .mjs, manual CLI parsing, local-only imports, schedule job string formatting, get_jobs length, and executable parity requirements.
serial.plan_and_ownership: One actor owned probing, implementation, verification, and delivery without delegation or shared-writer boundaries.
serial.implementation: Implemented lib/cli/argparse.mjs, lib/schedule/job.mjs, scheduler.mjs, index.mjs, and test12.mjs in one coherent patch.
serial.integration_and_delivery: The entrypoint imported the local parser and schedule index; there was no cross-agent merge or duplicate module cleanup before final delivery.
serial.verification: Ran executable probes, Node runs for normal/help/error paths, a stdout diff for normal execution, and checked sampled argparse behaviors before final response.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: No official unfinished requirement remained; final official evaluation passed 150 of 150.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel addressed the required ESM .mjs files, manual argv parsing, local-only modules, schedule API behavior, exact stdout, and black-box executable probing.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial addressed the same required ESM .mjs files, manual argv parsing, local-only modules, schedule API behavior, exact stdout, and black-box executable probing.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No requirement coverage difference affected the result; both recognized and satisfied the task, though parallel sampled more edge cases through child work.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel split probing and implementation across parent, first child, and nested child, but both parent and first child touched implementation files.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial used a single-thread plan: probe, build modules, add entry file, and verify.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had overlapping implementation ownership, while serial kept file ownership centralized.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel handoffs were enough for useful probing and implementation, but file-interface ownership for the generated entrypoint and helper modules was not cleanly separated.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no child handoff or cross-agent interface boundary; the same actor carried task knowledge from probes into implementation.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel introduced a coordination boundary around shared files; serial avoided that boundary entirely.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel produced two implementation shapes, then converged on python_int.mjs, argparse_compat.mjs, scheduler/job/index modules, and test12.mjs.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial produced argparse.mjs plus scheduler/job/index modules and test12.mjs in a single coherent implementation path.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both final implementations were accepted, but parallel needed extra patching after the overlapping child implementation appeared.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Nested probe and first child both completed and their results became visible to the parent; the parent received the child final and continued integration.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no delegated result lifecycle and proceeded directly from local verification to final response.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had additional child-result retrieval and reconciliation steps; serial had none.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parent found a conflicting implementation in /output, patched the active implementation, and deleted duplicate unused modules before closure.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial produced one file tree and did not report conflicting generated modules or cleanup.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had concrete shared-state reconciliation; serial avoided shared-state conflict.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel ran Node checks, fixed mismatches, reran a comparison harness to OK, and the official evaluator passed 150 of 150.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial ran Node checks, a normal stdout diff, sampled parser cases, and the official evaluator passed 150 of 150.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both had sufficient acceptance evidence and official success; parallel had extra post-reconciliation verification.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel used three subagents and 536 agent seconds, but did not time out and closed only after cleanup and verification.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial used no subagents and 263 agent seconds, did not time out, and closed after direct verification.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel consumed substantially more process budget because of delegation and reconciliation, but the extra work did not prevent a complete passing deliverable.

outcome_analysis.explanation: The current official evaluation is not discordant: both parallel and serial completed and passed all 150 samples. The substantive difference is that the parallel run introduced overlapping child/parent writes and then repaired the shared output tree, while the serial run produced and verified one coherent implementation path.
parallel_contributors: Delegation produced extra probing and an independently written implementation that the parent later reconciled.
Parent cleanup and post-reconciliation checks converted the parallel churn into a passing artifact.
serial_contributors: Single-owner implementation avoided cross-agent file conflicts.
Serial verification covered normal output and sampled CLI error behavior before final response.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Parallel final code used python_int.mjs and argparse_compat.mjs, while serial used one argparse.mjs helper; both satisfied the evaluator.
Parallel sampled and normalized more CLI edge cases but that did not create a score difference.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: no outcome difference; retained pattern is a parallel adverse process consequence only
